desc: Parse the inputs: read integer \(N\), coordinates \(R, C\), and the string \(S\) of length \(N\).
Initialize the current position at \((0,0)\) and a set `seen` containing \(\{(0,0)\}\).
Iterate over the characters of \(S\) from index \(0\) to \(N-1\), updating the current position according to the direction (N, W, S, E).

For each time step \(t = 1, \dots, N\), compute `target = (current_row - R, current_col - C)`. If `target` is in `seen`, append `'1'` to the result; otherwise append `'0'`. Then add the current position to `seen`.
Debug the failure on sample 2: manually compute prefix sums, generation times, and smoke positions for each t, and compare with the expected output.

Re-derive the necessary condition: smoke exists at (R,C) at time t+0.5 iff there exists a generation time g < t such that P[t] - P[g] = (R,C). This is equivalent to P[t] - (R,C) being in the set of prefix sums at generation times up to t-1.
Test the corrected algorithm on sample 2 and sample 3.

Implement the corrected algorithm: maintain a set of generation prefix sums, adding P[t] when t is a generation time (first occurrence of a distinct prefix sum). For each t, check if P[t] - (R,C) is in that set.
Run the implementation on all sample inputs and confirm correct outputs.
